They have 5 health per segment, making all pickaxes equally good at mining them. == Availability == Besides being found in the Sunken Crypts, they can also rarely be found underground in the Swamp. Generally, the player will need a [[Wishbone]] to find these deposits. However, due to these nodes extending below the water line, it can be challenging to effectively mine them. When mined, they uniquely do not guarantee resources but instead have a small chance of dropping [[Scrap Iron]], [[Leather Scraps]] or [[Withered Bone]]s. == Drops == In Sunken Crypts, Muddy Scrap Piles have 30 segments and each segment may drop the following when mined: {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Scrap Iron|amt=1|rate=14.29%
(avg. 4.3 per pile)}} {{loot row|item=Leather Scraps|amt=1|rate=2.86%
(avg. 0.86 per pile)}} {{loot row|item=Withered Bone|amt=1|rate=2.86%
(avg. 0.86 per pile)}} }} The Muddy Scrap Piles found outdoors in the Swamp have 20 segments, each segment may drop: {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Scrap Iron|amt=1|rate=29.7%
(avg. 6 per pile)}} {{loot row|item=Withered Bone|amt=1|rate=0.3%
(avg. 0.06 per pile)}} }} == Notes == * Metal deposits do not respawn. * Muddy Scrap Piles are the only metal resource currently in the game not to guarantee items upon being mined. * Like other metals, the resulting Scrap iron cannot be teleported through a [[Portal|Wood portal]] * Enemies or [[Body Pile|Body Piles]] on the other side of a Muddy Scrap Pile can be safely damaged or destroyed by the AoE effect from a 2-handed mace such as the [[Stagbreaker]] or the [[Iron Sledge]], without damaging the Muddy Scrap Pile itself. [[Ancient Armor]] | usage = Smelting | buy = | sell = | weight = 10.0 | stack = 30 | teleport = No }} '''Scrap Iron''' is a raw metal that can be turned into [[Iron]] in a [[Smelter]] using [[Coal]] as fuel. == Availability == In the [[Swamp]], its primary source are [[Sunken Crypts]]. There, it can be mined from [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s using any pickaxe, or found inside [[Chest]]s. The [[Swamp Key]], obtained from the [[Elder]], has to be obtained to access Sunken Crypts. Alternatively, Muddy scrap piles can be found underground in Swamps. However, these are scarce, and ultimately yield little Iron scrap. They can be located using a [[Wishbone]] or by using the [[How to play#How_to_prospect_properly?|Prospecting]] method with a [[Stagbreaker]] or Weapons with the same attack ([[Iron Sledge]]). [[Oozer]]s can also rarely drop Scrap iron with a drop rate of around 30%. Later in the game, Iron and [[Copper Scrap]] can be obtained by mining [[Ancient Sword]]s and [[Ancient Armor]] in the [[Mistlands]]. == Notes == * Like other metals, Scrap Iron cannot be teleported without a [[Portal stone]]. * Scrap iron ore is 2 units lighter than smelted Iron. {{MaterialsNav}} [[ru:Металлолом]] [[cs:Železný šrot]] [[uk:Металобрухт]] [[de:Eisenschrott]] [[fr:Ferraille]]

The '''Spinning Wheel''' is a crafting station which converts {{Item link|Flax}} into {{Item link|Linen Thread}}. Each piece of Flax takes 30 seconds to convert into Linen thread. It has a capacity of 40 Flax, and will drop Linen as it is made automatically.

The Spinning Wheel becomes available after the player has killed [[Moder]] to obtain the materials for an [[Artisan Table]]. It must be placed within the radius of the Artisan Table, but does not require it to function after placement.

'''Poison''' is a negative [[status effect]] that applies a damage overtime effect on the affected entity. It is caused by [[Damage types#Poison|Poison damage]].

All resistances like [[Poison Resistance Mead]] are applied at the time of creating the effect and ignored on tick. Therefore any change to resistances after the effect start doesn't change it.

=== Stacking ===
Poison damage does not stack. The effect calculates how much damage remains to be dealt, and if a new poisonous attacks deals more poison damage than the remaining one, the effect is re-created. Otherwise, that incoming damage is ignored.

== Calculations ==
Duration from total damage is calculated (see below for more precise numbers) as <math>\lceil (1 + \sqrt{X*damage}) \rceil</math> where X is 5 against players and 1 against enemies. This means Poison lasts roughly twice as long for players and halves the tick damage. See further section for the technical details.

Tick damage is calculated with <math>{total \ damage \over duration}</math>.

=== Extra damage ===
Theoretically, the total damage from all ticks should be the same as initial value, but due to rounding the total damage is slightly higher.

* First we take non-integer value of <math>duration</math> as: <math>1 + \sqrt{X*damage}</math>
* then we take <math>damagePerHit = \frac{totalDamage}{\lfloor duration \rfloor}</math>
* then actual number of ticks is <math>\lfloor \frac{duration}{1.02} \rfloor + 1</math>.

Where does this come from? Due to floating number peculiarities<ref>https://0.30000000000000004.com/</ref> and the fact, that Valheim runs physics on fixed 50 FPS, every tick takes 1.02 seconds, but since first tick happens at the beginning of duration, when time = 0, we have an extra one.

Here's a table with calculations for various damage values: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSrjL9LtSGBgIAgr7Y_9Kej79ZQ9bh70ND9pNOAeCA5axUGA-AEp4FKdGhra-co-8RdeMpB5TLrlsV-/pubhtml Poison damage google spreadsheets].

An '''Obsidian Deposit''' is a resource node and is found in the [[Mountain]]s biome and require an [[Iron Pickaxe]] or better to harvest.

== Availability ==
Obsidian Deposits appear as small, sphere-shaped rocks with distinct black colored veins, which help differentiate them from regular rocks at a distance. They yield [[Obsidian]] when mined.

They are only found on the surface.

== Drops ==
{{loot table|
{{loot row|item=Obsidian|amt=5-8|rate=100%}}
}}

== Notes ==
* Obsidian Deposits do not respawn.
* Unlike other resources that require mining, Obsidian can be teleported.

'''Damage''' is a reduction of an entity's health points. It affects much of the core gameplay mechanics. [[Creatures]] have innate resistances and weaknesses but are also affected by some [[status effects]]. Players may acquire resistances and weaknesses from [[armor]], [[Mead|meads]] or [[status effects]]. [[#Creature Resistance Matrix|At the bottom]] of this page is a chart of creature Weaknesses, Resistances and Immunities. '''Chain lightning''' is an on-hit effect triggered by weapons upgraded with [[Iolite]] or [[Thunderblood Essence]].

==Effect==
Chain lightning has a 25% chance to trigger on a normal attack and a 20% chance to trigger on a secondary attack.

It deals 75 [[lightning]] damage to the target, the amount is not affected by skills, and it cannot be blocked or dodged.

Once triggered, it has an 80% chance of bouncing off nearby enemies or players. If so, each nearby target within 8 meters has a 30% chance of being targeted, up to a maximum of 2–4 targets per bounce (the maximum is chosen at random then targets are processed starting from the nearest). The process repeats indefinitely, centered on each new target, but with the chance of rebound multiplied by 0.75 each time (i.e., 80% → 60% → 45% → 33.75%, etc.).

A single activation of chain lightning cannot affect the same target more than once.

==Notes==
* Chain lightning within the vicinity of neutral [[Ashlands Dvergr]] has the potential of damaging them, immediately turning them hostile.

The '''Grappling Hook''' is a [[Mistlands]]-tier tool used for traversal.

== Availability ==
All ingredients for a Grappling Hook can be obtained in the Mistlands. Particularly, the {{Item link|Hook}} can be found in [[Infested Mine]]s, ruined [[Dvergr Guard Tower]]s and on the top of [[Rock Spire]]s.

It cannot be upgraded.

== Recipe ==
The Grappling Hook is crafted at a level 1 [[Black Forge]] with:
* {{Item link|Yggdrasil Wood|10}}
* {{Item link|Refined Eitr|10}}
* {{Item link|Mandible|4}}
* {{Item link|Hook|1}}

== Usage ==
The hook can be shot in a limited range (just over 40 meters), and then retracted. It is particularly useful for traversing the craggy Mistlands terrain.

Both the primary and the secondary attack fire a hook projectile, and each costs 15 [[Stamina]].

Caution should be taken to avoid lethal fall damage; a {{Item link|Feather Cape}} can be worn to prevent it.

'''Frigid Kiln''' is a structure used to produce {{Item link|Liquid Frost}} out of {{Item link|Ice}}. Liquid Frost is the fuel of the [[Frost Foundry]].

==Availability==
* {{Item link|Frostcore}} can be obtained from [[Winding Tunnels]].
* {{Item link|Ice}} can be obtained by mining [[Ice Sheet]]s on the shore of the [[Deep North]], or dropped from [[Greydwarf (Deep North)|Greydwarfs]] in the Deep North

==Building==
The Frigid Kiln is found in the Crafting category of the [[Hammer]] and requires a nearby [[Workbench]] to build. It cannot be placed on wood, in water or on sloped surfaces. It costs:
* {{Item link|Stone|20}}
* {{Item link|Frostcore|10}}
* {{Item link|Ice|5}}

It has 1,500 durability. It is resistant to blunt, pierce, slash and chop damage, and immune to fire, frost, poison and spirit damage.

==Usage==
Ice is the kiln's only input; it is added like fuel, and no other item is needed. The kiln holds up to 25 [[Ice]] at a time. It produces one [[Liquid Frost]] every 30 seconds by consuming five Ice, so a full load of 25 Ice becomes five Liquid Frost in 150 seconds. Each Liquid Frost is ejected as soon as it is made.

Like the [[Smelter]], the Frigid Kiln stops working while its smoke is blocked.
